task.chat.title: Assistant and rewriting
task.chat.huggingfacetb-smollm3-3b: A 3B model with two thinking modes. For short replies, choose non-thinking mode and an explicit output budget.
task.chat.coherelabs-aya-expanse-8b: Declares 23 languages, including Persian and Spanish; 8,192-token context and a noncommercial public licence.
task.rag.title: Answers from documents
task.rag.qwen-qwen3-4b: Smaller generator with selectable thinking. Retrieval is a separate component; document chunks consume the context budget.
task.rag.qwen-qwen3-8b: A larger option in the same family. Compare its Q4 and Q8 packages and context-dependent KV requirements in the memory view.
task.embedding.title: Embedding and retrieval
task.embedding.intfloat-multilingual-e5-: Small multilingual encoder with a 512-token limit; query: and passage: prefixes also apply to non-English text.
Larger instruction-aware model with 1,024-dimensional vectors; task instruction on the query, still a 512-token limit.
task.reranking.title: Rerank retrieved results
task.reranking.baai-bge-reranker-v2-m3: Scores query–document pairs; it does not produce stored embeddings. Check evidence for the selected language separately from its multilingual declaration.
task.reranking.qwen-qwen3-reranker-0-6b: Instruction-aware 0.6B reranker; preserve its yes/no template and model-specific scoring path.
task.json.title: Field extraction and JSON
task.json.qwen-qwen3-4b-instruct-2507: Instruct-only variant without thinking mode; grammar-constrained output and schema validation also require engine and application support.
task.completion.title: Editor code completion
task.completion.qwen-qwen2-5-coder-1-5b: Base model with FIM for text before and after the cursor; it is not a ready-to-use chat assistant or agent.
task.completion.bigcode-starcoder2-3b: 3B base model with FIM; compare accepted completions, latency and the actual programming language.
task.coding-agent.title: Coding assistant and agent
task.coding-agent.qwen-qwen3-coder-30b-a: MoE with 30B total and about 3B active parameters; memory planning still includes all weights.
task.coding-agent.qwen-qwen3-coder-next: 80B model with about 3B active parameters and hybrid attention; the guide’s conventional KV formula does not cover its complete memory requirements.
task.reasoning.title: Reasoning and problem solving
task.reasoning.deepseek-ai-deepseek-r1-d: Smaller distilled variant in a common publisher table. MATH-500 is in English; its score is not Persian or Spanish evidence.
Larger variant under the same reported protocol; compare reasoning-token budgets and artifact formats alongside scores.
task.vision.title: Documents and images
task.vision.qwen-qwen3-vl-8b-instruct: Vision-language variant; a text-only model cannot replace it. Image count and resolution affect inputs and memory.
task.vision.google-gemma-3-4b-it: Smaller text-and-image option; text benchmark scores do not establish OCR or chart-understanding quality.

LlmGuidePage.1024: Running a language model on your own computer or server can support chat, coding, translation or answers grounded in documents. Data confidentiality, control over service dependencies and predictable costs are common reasons to consider local deployment. The range of models and execution methods makes the choice less straightforward: which model is sufficient for the task, what fits the available hardware, and when does upgrading the infrastructure make a useful difference?
LlmGuidePage.1025: This guide brings those decisions together. Its interactive tables compare small and large language models, related specialist models, hardware requirements and runtime software, with links to the supporting sources. The accompanying articles explain the practical advantages and limits of each approach, connecting the task and required quality to the resources and budget needed to deliver it.

method.title: Sources and coverage
method.sources: Specifications come from model cards, configurations and versioned software documentation. Quality and speed results retain their reporter and source conditions; this site has not run independent model benchmarks.
method.selection: Candidates cover distinct roles: text generation, coding, images and documents, embedding and reranking. Model size and a multilingual label do not replace evidence for the selected task and language.
method.hardware: The hardware table and most current speed reports focus on NVIDIA. CPU, Apple Silicon and AMD execution depends on the software and backend; the guide lacks matched speed results for ranking all these platforms.
method.memory: Memory estimates combine weight-file bytes, KV and a reserve for each device. The conventional KV formula is not applied to hybrid, MLA or unknown architectures. Assumptions are available in the memory section.
method.correction: Report a correction through the résumé contact links
quality.reference-policy: This collection permits only scoped within-report comparisons; see the evidence panel.
reference.methodology.title: How selection and comparison work
reference.methodology.intro: This guide brings published evaluations and technical documentation together to support model and tool selection. Quality, latency and memory figures retain their reporter and reported conditions. The site has not run new model experiments.
reference.methodology.comparisonNotice: Two displayed numbers are not automatically rankable. Check the model variant, benchmark version, language, generation mode and protocol. A reported score difference is neither a quality ratio nor a statistical-significance claim.
